[.claude/skills/modeler/SKILL.md#tool-selection]

## Tool Selection

| Diagram Type | Tool | Output | When |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **ER / Data Model** | Mermaid `erDiagram` | Inline in markdown | Default for all data modeling |
| **Sequence diagram** | Mermaid `sequenceDiagram` | Inline in markdown | Interaction flows, API calls |
| **Flowchart** | Mermaid `graph TD/LR` | Inline in markdown | Process flows, decision trees |
| **State machine** | Mermaid `stateDiagram-v2` | Inline in markdown | Lifecycle states, workflow states |
| **Class diagram** | Mermaid `classDiagram` | Inline in markdown | Domain models, aggregate roots |
| **C4 Context (L1)** | Mermaid `graph TD` or Draw.io | Inline or `.drawio` + `.svg` | System context — simple = Mermaid, complex = Draw.io |
| **C4 Container (L2)** | Draw.io | `.drawio` + `.svg` in `assets/` | Container topology — too dense for Mermaid |
| **C4 Component (L3)** | Draw.io | `.drawio` + `.svg` in `assets/` | Component internals — needs precise layout |
| **Complex topology** | Draw.io | `.drawio` + `.svg` in `assets/` | Multi-layer architecture with 20+ shapes |

**Default to Mermaid.** Only use Draw.io when the diagram exceeds ~40 lines of Mermaid, needs precise positioning, or requires shapes Mermaid can't render (cylinders, clouds, shields).

[.claude/skills/modeler/SKILL.md#no-forced-aspect-ratio]

## No Forced Aspect Ratio

Unlike the `/presenter` skill, modeler diagrams have **no mandatory aspect ratio**. Diagrams size to their content. Draw.io canvases are set to fit content, not to 1920×1080.

[.claude/skills/modeler/SKILL.md#er-diagrams-mermaid-erdiagram]

### ER Diagrams (Mermaid `erDiagram`)

Use Mermaid ER diagrams for all data model visuals in documentation.

**Naming conventions:**

| Element | Convention | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entity names | PascalCase (DDD aggregate name) | `ClaimHeader`, `ProviderEnrollment` |
| Table names | snake_case (physical) | `claim_header`, `provider_enrollment` |
| Attributes | snake_case | `claim_id`, `submitted_date` |
| Primary keys | Suffix with `PK` type | `claim_id UUID PK` |
| Foreign keys | Suffix with `FK` type | `provider_id UUID FK` |

**Relationship notation:**

| Symbol | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `\|\|--o{` | One to many |
| `\|\|--\|\|` | One to one |
| `o{--o{` | Many to many |
| `\|\|--o\|` | One to zero-or-one |

**Required elements in every ER diagram:**

- All entities with their key attributes (PK, FK, and 3-5 most important business attributes)
- All relationships with cardinality
- Relationship labels that describe the business meaning (e.g., "submits", "adjudicates", "covers")

**Example:**

```mermaid
erDiagram
    Provider ||--o{ Claim : "submits"
    Claim ||--|| ClaimStatus : "has"
    Claim ||--o{ ClaimLine : "contains"
    Member ||--o{ Claim : "is subject of"

    Provider {
        uuid provider_id PK
        string npi
        string name
        string taxonomy_code
        date enrollment_date
    }

    Claim {
        uuid claim_id PK
        uuid provider_id FK
        uuid member_id FK
        string claim_type
        date service_date
        decimal total_amount
    }

    ClaimLine {
        uuid line_id PK
        uuid claim_id FK
        string procedure_code
        decimal amount
        int units
    }

    Member {
        uuid member_id PK
        string medicaid_id
        string first_name
        string last_name
        date dob
    }

    ClaimStatus {
        uuid status_id PK
        uuid claim_id FK
        string status
        timestamp updated_at
    }
```

[.claude/skills/modeler/SKILL.md#domain-model-diagrams-mermaid-classdiagram]

### Domain Model Diagrams (Mermaid `classDiagram`)

Use class diagrams for DDD domain models showing aggregates, entities, and value objects:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class ClaimAggregate {
        <<Aggregate Root>>
        +UUID claimId
        +submit()
        +adjudicate()
        +deny(reason)
    }

    class ClaimLine {
        <<Entity>>
        +UUID lineId
        +String procedureCode
        +Decimal amount
    }

    class Money {
        <<Value Object>>
        +Decimal amount
        +String currency
    }

    ClaimAggregate "1" *-- "1..*" ClaimLine
    ClaimLine *-- Money
```

[.claude/skills/modeler/SKILL.md#sequence-diagrams]

### Sequence Diagrams

Use for API interaction flows, event-driven workflows, and integration patterns:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant Gateway as API Gateway
    participant Service as Claims Service
    participant DB as Aurora DB
    participant Kafka as Event Fabric

    Client->>Gateway: POST /claims
    Gateway->>Service: Forward (mTLS)
    Service->>DB: INSERT claim
    DB-->>Service: claim_id
    Service->>Kafka: ClaimSubmitted event
    Service-->>Gateway: 201 Created
    Gateway-->>Client: claim_id
```

[.claude/skills/modeler/SKILL.md#flowcharts-mermaid-graph]

### Flowcharts (Mermaid `graph`)

Use `graph TD` (top-down) for hierarchical flows, `graph LR` (left-right) for sequential processes.

| Direction | When to Use |
| --- | --- |
| `graph TD` | Decision trees, org hierarchies, data flow from top to bottom |
| `graph LR` | Sequential pipelines, request flows, left-to-right timelines |

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[Claim Submitted] --> B{Valid?}
    B -->|Yes| C[Adjudicate]
    B -->|No| D[Reject]
    C --> E{Rules Pass?}
    E -->|Yes| F[Approve & Pay]
    E -->|No| G[Deny]
    G --> H[Generate Denial Notice]
    F --> I[Generate Payment]
```

[.claude/skills/modeler/SKILL.md#state-machines-mermaid-statediagram-v2]

### State Machines (Mermaid `stateDiagram-v2`)

Use for entity lifecycle states and workflow transitions:

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Submitted
    Submitted --> InReview : assign_reviewer
    InReview --> Approved : approve
    InReview --> Denied : deny
    InReview --> PendingInfo : request_info
    PendingInfo --> InReview : info_received
    Approved --> Paid : process_payment
    Denied --> Appeal : member_appeals
    Appeal --> InReview : reopen
    Paid --> [*]
```

[.claude/skills/modeler/SKILL.md#event-storming--domain-events-mermaid-graph-lr]

### Event Storming / Domain Events (Mermaid `graph LR`)

Use for mapping domain events in CQRS/event-sourced systems. Color-code by type:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph Commands
        C1[SubmitClaim]
        C2[AdjudicateClaim]
        C3[DenyClaim]
    end
    subgraph Events
        E1[ClaimSubmitted]
        E2[ClaimAdjudicated]
        E3[ClaimDenied]
        E4[PaymentIssued]
    end
    subgraph Read Models
        R1[ClaimStatusView]
        R2[PaymentLedgerView]
    end

    C1 --> E1
    C2 --> E2
    C2 --> E4
    C3 --> E3
    E1 --> R1
    E2 --> R1
    E3 --> R1
    E4 --> R2
```

[.claude/skills/modeler/SKILL.md#deployment--infrastructure-mermaid-graph-td]

### Deployment / Infrastructure (Mermaid `graph TD`)

Use for basic AWS topology when Draw.io is overkill:

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph VPC["AWS VPC"]
        subgraph Public["Public Subnet"]
            ALB[Application Load Balancer]
        end
        subgraph Private["Private Subnet"]
            EKS[EKS Cluster]
            RDS[(Aurora PostgreSQL)]
            REDIS[(ElastiCache Redis)]
        end
    end

    Users --> ALB
    ALB --> EKS
    EKS --> RDS
    EKS --> REDIS
    EKS --> MSK[Amazon MSK / Kafka]
    EKS --> S3[(S3 Storage)]
    EKS --> Bedrock[AWS Bedrock]
```

[.claude/skills/modeler/SKILL.md#theme--colors]

### Theme & Colors

Use the `default` Mermaid theme — do not apply custom Mermaid theme overrides. However, when choosing colors for subgraphs, notes, or highlights, reference `.claude/templates/diagram-style-guide.md` for the brand color palette. This keeps Mermaid diagrams visually consistent with Draw.io diagrams produced by `/presenter`.

Key colors from the style guide for Mermaid use:

- **Primary blue:** `#2435C7` — headers, emphasis
- **Cyan:** `#00B9D8` — mid-tier, secondary
- **Green:** `#00C49A` — success, new/modern
- **Orange:** `#e67e22` — warnings, events
- **Red:** `#c0392b` — critical, legacy
- **Charcoal:** `#2b3a44` — text, labels
- **Gray:** `#5a6978` — secondary text

[.claude/skills/modeler/SKILL.md#size-limits]

### Size Limits

| Lines | Action |
| --- | --- |
| **< 20** | Perfect for Mermaid — inline, focused |
| **20-40** | Acceptable — may need to split if readability suffers |
| **40-60** | Consider splitting into 2 diagrams or switching to Draw.io |
| **> 60** | Switch to Draw.io — Mermaid becomes unreadable at this size |

When splitting, each sub-diagram should be self-contained with a clear title and scope.

[.claude/skills/modeler/SKILL.md#architecture-diagram-standards]

## Architecture Diagram Standards

When using Draw.io for complex architecture diagrams:

- **Read `.claude/templates/diagram-style-guide.md`** for colors and fonts — same palette as presenter
- **No forced 16:9** — canvas sizes to content
- **Header optional** — use gradient header only if the diagram will also appear in a deck
- **Lighter density** — more whitespace than deck diagrams; optimize for readability at various zoom levels
- **Export SVG** — always `--svg-theme light`, placed in `assets/` alongside the `.drawio`

[.claude/skills/modeler/SKILL.md#one-diagram-per-bounded-context]

## One Diagram Per Bounded Context

Data models should be scoped to a single bounded context. If a diagram starts showing entities from multiple domains, split it.

| Scope | ER Diagram |
| --- | --- |
| Claims domain | `claims-data-model.md` contains Claims ER |
| Provider domain | `provider-data-model.md` contains Provider ER |
| Cross-domain relationships | Show as external references (dashed lines) to the other domain's aggregate root only |

[.claude/skills/modeler/SKILL.md#file-organization]

## File Organization

| Output | Location |
| --- | --- |
| Mermaid diagrams | Inline in the markdown file — no separate file |
| Draw.io source | `assets/` subfolder under the referencing doc folder |
| Draw.io SVG export | Same `assets/` folder alongside the `.drawio` |

[.claude/skills/modeler/SKILL.md#skill-collaboration]

## Skill Collaboration

| Collaborator | Relationship |
| --- | --- |
| **architect** | Architect defines what to model — aggregates, boundaries, relationships. Architect always uses modeler directly. |
| **documenter** | Documenter embeds Mermaid output in documentation. Routes through `/diagrammer` if deck visuals needed. |
| **business-analyst** | BA provides domain language and entity relationships. Modeler renders ER diagrams from BA specs. |
| **presenter** | If a technical diagram needs to become a deck visual, the user invokes `/diagrammer` which routes to `/presenter`. Modeler never calls presenter directly. |
